documents.title: Responsible AI Use at UCF: Ethical Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The page says "Students should look to individual syllabi for guidance on how, when, and if AI use is permitted" and that UCF has no AI-specific policy "as yet", so it sets no default for students beyond disclosure and integrity rules and hands the decision to instructors.
documents.summary: UCF's AI for All initiative lists ethical guidelines: disclosure of AI use, no uploading of copyrighted material, vetting for deepfakes and hallucinations, and separate rules for students, faculty teaching and research, and staff. Whether students may use AI is left to each syllabus; faculty are told to avoid detectors and not to grade by AI alone.

units.policy: The intentional use of AI-assisted tools for any element of a work or school product must be disclosed

units.frag_start: As a contractor of the FAA, UCF

documents.title: Ethical Use of AI (students)
documents.stance_why: The page says "its use should be avoided unless explicitly permitted by the instructor", which sets a default of no AI use unless an instructor allows it. It also says "Students must embrace the inevitable changes" and recommends Copilot-Chat, but that is encouragement to build AI skill and does not change the course-work default. Wording is advisory ("should be avoided"), so restrict rather than prohibit.
documents.summary: A student-facing page that mixes encouragement (AI fluency for careers, official Copilot-Chat with data protection) with a default that AI be avoided unless an instructor permits it. It stresses checking the syllabus, verifying output, and owning AI errors.

units.why: The page says "Students must embrace the inevitable changes, and, moreover, become proficient users of AI to remain competitive"; an expectation grounded in professional skill, P44.
units.anchor: Students must embrace the inevitable changes, and, moreover, become proficient users of AI
units.frag_end: to remain competitive in the workplace.

units.anchor: the person who knows how to use AI will replace you
units.frag_start: “AI is not going to replace you.
units.policy: The page quotes: "AI is not going to replace you. But the person who knows how to use AI will replace you."
units.fit_note: A quoted slogan, not a rule. | Rhetorical quote used to motivate AI skill-building.

units.frag_start: The official AI tool at UCF

units.resolution_why: Coder A coded actor student and modality informs, coder B actor all and modality should; type P92 and phase agree. The page is addressed to students and the heading says "Recommended", so the sentence recommends rather than only informs. Final: actor student, modality should. The normalized policy keeps "official" and "Recommended" and does not say other tools are banned.

notes: Both documents are university-layer pages from UCF's AI for All initiative and neither is an official policy; the first states there is no AI-specific university policy yet. No school or computing documents were collected and the course layer is deferred. The career-planning units (AI portfolio, asking AI for target-occupation skillsets) are UNCOVERED and may recur at other universities as a career-readiness type. The no-AI-policy-yet statement is UNCOVERED. A pointer to a separate student advice page (coder B only) was dropped as navigation. Reconciled from coders A and B.
